hypothesis: Forcing fork start semantics before loading the unmodified evaluator will eliminate Python 3.14's forkserver dynamic-module import failure and allow the exact pinned primary taxi metric to be scored.
rationale: The WSL2 environment reaches the evaluator and metric but fails only when Python 3.14 forkserver workers re-import the dynamically loaded candidate module. A small external run wrapper can set fork before the evaluator is imported, preserving the pinned evaluator and metric source while changing only process-start compatibility.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether the exact primary k-server evaluator is operational in WSL and whether the upstream optimized example reproduces the reported three-violation scale.
method: Invoke research_tools/run_kserver_evaluator_fork.py, which sets multiprocessing start method to fork and then runpy-loads the unmodified pinned tools/evaluator/evaluate.py. Use the same upstream optimized evader example, kwargs, taxi metric, one final evaluator process, and persistent WSL virtualenv as kserver-baseline-reproduction-002.
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A result below 3 on the frozen primary metric is finite-evaluator progress toward the target but is not a proof of the full k-server conjecture; a result at 3 establishes baseline reproduction only.

configuration.runtime: WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04; Python 3.14 persistent virtualenv; fork start method

kill_condition: Stop after the first reproducible evaluator result or a precise runtime/metric/contract blocker; do not modify upstream evaluator or metric files to bypass failures.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: reproduces the upstream human-designed 17-violation baseline; does not reproduce the separately reported 3-violation result

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: runtime is now operational; this candidate is above the reported best and is not target progress

interpretation: The external fork wrapper made the unmodified pinned evaluator operational under WSL2 Python 3.14. The exact upstream parametrized example scored 17 violations on the frozen taxi metric, matching the README's human-designed baseline but not the separately reported 3-violation candidate. This is a primary-evaluator baseline result, not a proof of the conjecture.
what_was_learned: The k-server evaluator/metric contract is executable under WSL2 with an external fork-start wrapper, and the published parametrized example is the 17-violation human baseline rather than the 3-violation candidate. The remaining gap is candidate provenance/search, not the previously observed process-start blocker.
recommended_next_action: Preregister one bounded run of the pinned upstream staged n=7 search pipeline, adapted only for the available WSL paths and fork-compatible process start, with the exact taxi metric as the final gate; stop at the first reproducible <3 result or at the time budget.
repetition_justification: This is a justified retry because experiment 002 isolated a Python 3.14 forkserver import failure. The wrapper changes process-start semantics before evaluator import without changing the pinned evaluator, metric, candidate, or mathematical contract.
